claims.promise: Sessions, rather than a standalone factory, create views; removed APIs have no compatibility shims.
IWebViewSession owns profile state and exposes view creation plus cache, cookie, and website-data clearing.
Factories explicitly create persistent sessions by profile path or ephemeral sessions.
IWebView provides stop, reload, close, loading, HTML loading, and asynchronous messaging; close is idempotent and suppresses callbacks.
WebViewPolicy decides navigation, popups, bridge access, permissions, downloads, external URLs, and message validation with typed decisions.
A host closes a view before releasing ownership and explicitly handles permitted popups.
LoadEvent exposes Started, Redirected, Committed, Finished, and Failed with URL, error, frame flag, and navigation id.
Navigation decisions distinguish Allow, Cancel, and OpenExternally and requests include URL, frame, user-action, and redirect context.
Main-frame lifecycle events are ordered by navigation id and stale navigation or script results are not reported as current.
Default navigation permits HTTPS and explicitly controlled file/app URLs while rejecting malformed, javascript, and unknown schemes; absent external handler cancels.
Popup policy runs before child creation, defaults to reject, and a missing host handler rejects.
Bridge authority is granted per committed trusted main-frame origin; subframes and external pages have no access.
Bridge envelopes enforce size, version, allowed type, schema, command allowlist, JSON-safe outbound serialization, and cancellation of stale callbacks.
Sensitive permissions and downloads default to deny; unsupported capabilities are reported rather than granted.
The common API contains only portable semantics and adds backend-specific features only through capability discovery.
macOS session views share a data store and process pool while retaining separate content controllers and delegates.
A permitted popup inherits its session but receives a fresh bridge authorization decision.
setHtml remains only with policy-approved base URL and the same origin bridge rules.
Policy callbacks run on the UI thread, do not outlive sessions, and no callbacks fire after close.
Tests cover policy, envelopes, generation invalidation, close, session behavior, lifecycle, rejection paths, and trusted bridge access; demo and docs use the new model.
